othersDoBetter.text: Constant Therapy reports a fully remote Phase II trial of its app against standard care in post-stroke aphasia (company-run).
Constant Therapy holds FDA Breakthrough Device designation (April 2020) for its speech app; this is review priority, not marketing authorization.
Constant Therapy has a separate Clinician App and clinician-built home programs; Bonet's report is a one-page share only.
Tactus offers 19 single-purpose apps by a certified SLP, with a cueing hierarchy and your own photos, bought once.
TalkPath is free and lists over 13,500 exercises, far more than Bonet.
Flint FitMi is an FDA-listed device with 4 published studies on FitMi and MusicGlove, including one randomised trial on FitMi.
Flint sells a remote program where a licensed therapist builds the plan and reviews data monthly ($99/month).
Years in market: not stated on the vendor pages we read, so no claim is made either way.

MintPad and RehaBoard not found on any Flint page; only FitMi, MusicGlove, Flex AFO, CT app, Remote Neuro Recovery.
FitMi uses sensor pucks, not a camera, and its FAQ says it cannot run on iPads.
TalkPath page does not mention clinician plans or reports; notes took those from the App Store listing, which could not be re-read.
Tactus Language Therapy 4-in-1 still US$89.99; other apps $9.99 to $29.99; one-time, no subscription.
Constant Therapy Breakthrough Device designation is on its own site; notes did not record it.
